subject.title: fix(synology-chat): handle HEAD probe and return 200 on webhook ACK

question: Should the Synology Chat webhook intentionally return unauthenticated 200 responses to HEAD liveness probes while keeping POST token validation and throttling unchanged?
rationale: Source shows this is the focused compatibility fix, but the tokenless HEAD response is a webhook boundary choice that automation should not silently accept without maintainer intent and real Synology proof.

options.title: Accept HEAD Liveness After Proof
options.body: Permit unauthenticated HEAD 200 for Synology compatibility, but require rebase plus redacted proof showing HEAD success, POST 200 {"success":true}, and continued message delivery before merge.

options.title: Require Authenticated Probe
options.body: Ask the contributor to prove Synology can send a token with its probe or choose a different liveness shape, reducing route-liveness exposure but risking the reported integration failure remains unfixed.

options.title: Replace The Stale Branch
options.body: If the contributor cannot refresh and prove the branch, close only after a narrow replacement PR preserves the useful fix and credits this source work.

recommendation.title: Accept HEAD Liveness After Proof
recommendation.body: Permit unauthenticated HEAD 200 for Synology compatibility, but require rebase plus redacted proof showing HEAD success, POST 200 {"success":true}, and continued message delivery before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Synology webhook and docs history makes this the best available routing candidate for the liveness/security-boundary choice.
